#table(stroke: none, columns: 2, align: (left, left, ), table.vline(stroke: .5pt, x: 0), table.vline(stroke: .5pt, x: 1), table.vline(stroke: .5pt, x: 2), table.hline(stroke: .5pt), [$t$ (seconds)], [$v(t)$ (feet per second)], table.hline(stroke: .5pt), [0], [0], table.hline(stroke: .5pt), [5], [12], table.hline(stroke: .5pt), [10], [20], table.hline(stroke: .5pt), [15], [30], table.hline(stroke: .5pt), [20], [55], table.hline(stroke: .5pt), [25], [70], table.hline(stroke: .5pt), [30], [78], table.hline(stroke: .5pt), [35], [81], table.hline(stroke: .5pt), [40], [75], table.hline(stroke: .5pt), [45], [60], table.hline(stroke: .5pt), [50], [72], table.hline(stroke: .5pt));

The graph of the velocity $v(t)$, in ft/sec, of a car traveling on a straight road, for $0 <= t <= 50$, is shown above. A table of values for $v(t)$, at 5 second intervals of time $t$, is shown to the right of the graph.

(a) During what intervals of time is the acceleration of the car positive? Give a reason for your answer.

(b) Find the average acceleration of the car, in $upright(f t) \/ upright(s e c)^(2)$, over the interval $0 <= t <= 50$.

(c) Find one approximation for the acceleration of the car, in $upright(f t) \/ upright(s e c)^(2)$, at $t = 40$. Show the computations you used to arrive at your answer.

(d) Approximate $integral_(0)^(50) v(t) d t$ with a Riemann sum, using the midpoints of five subintervals of equal length. Using correct units, explain the meaning of this integral.
